bullets.title: Iran-Hormuz Escalation Spikes Oil 9%+, Raises Rate Hike Odds to 40-50%
bullets.body: US launched third consecutive night of Iran strikes targeting Hormuz-related military infrastructure; Trump proposed a 20% cargo toll on Strait transits and reinstated naval blockade effective July 14 at 4PM ET. Brent crude settled up ~9.6% at $83.30/bbl and WTI rose 9.4% to $78.14, the largest single-day gain since 2020. Markets now price 40-50% probability of a July 29 Fed hike (vs. sub-10% earlier in the month), with Jefferies flagging a potential shift from geopolitical risk to stagflation/monetary shock as freight, insurance, and refined-product markets price in sustained Hormuz disruption.

bullets.title: June CPI Print the Day's Macro Fulcrum: Core MoM 0.2% = Base Case; 0.3% = July Hike
bullets.body: Consensus expects headline CPI -0.1% MoM (gasoline collapse) and core +0.22% MoM (~2.8% YoY). Multiple desks frame it as binary: core above 0.25% triggers hawkish repricing and lifts July hike odds further, while 0.21% or below would be dovish and support momentum recovery. Options market is pricing only ~70bps SPX move vs. a typical 1-1.1%, suggesting micro/earnings are dominating attention heading into the print. Fed Chair Warsh's first congressional testimony (9AM ET) is the other key catalyst of the day.

bullets.title: IBM -22% Pre-Market Triggers Broad Software Selloff; Enterprise IT Capex Rotating to Servers/Storage
bullets.body: IBM pre-announced Q2 revenue of $17.20B vs. $17.86B consensus and EPS $2.93 vs. $3.01, citing clients shifting quarterly capex to servers, storage, and memory ahead of AI-driven price increases, plus large deals failing to close. The miss dragged enterprise software broadly lower in pre-market: WDAY -8.9%, HUBS -8.9%, NOW -7.8%, CRM -6.1%, SNOW -4.7%, MDB -4.4%, ADBE -5.5%, PLTR -5.2%. Analysts across UBS, JPM, and GS describe the shift as capex reprioritization rather than demand destruction, with cybersecurity distracting enterprise budgets further.

bullets.title: Semi/Memory Pullback: SOX -4.8%, Momentum Factor Worst 3-Week Drawdown Since 2000
bullets.body: SK Hynix's 15% plunge in Seoul (recovering 6%) triggered a broad semis selloff; SOX fell 4.78% and the Tech Momentum index is now in its 6th day of a 20%+ drawdown, historically the sharpest since the early 2000s. Multiple desks (OPCO, JPM, GS) characterize the move as positioning-driven froth coming out—TSMC June revenue was +68% and memory fundamentals remain structurally tight into 2027—but acknowledge the question is whether the washout is sufficient to set up the next buyable dip. SMH 1M implied vol hit 99th percentile at 55.9 despite investors remaining net bullish into earnings.

bullets.title: BofA Fund Manager Survey: Extreme Bull Positioning, Cash at 3.6%, Semis Most Crowded Trade
bullets.body: BofA's latest survey shows cash levels at ultra-low 3.6% and 82% of investors view long global semis as the most crowded trade. Top 10 stocks represent 40%+ of S&P 500 market cap. Announced buybacks hit $2T in 2026 but actual executions are tracking only ~$650B, the widest execution gap since 2018. Momentum factor suffered one of its sharpest 3-week pullbacks on record after years of AI-driven leadership.

bullets.title: Consumer Spending Accelerates for 7th Straight Month; $51B Wallet Tailwind Ahead
bullets.body: JPM card data shows June US consumer spending +5.7% YoY with acceleration across all income cohorts: upper +7.1%, middle +6.9%, lower +4.9%. Discretionary spending rose 6.1% YoY in June, up 110bps vs. May. Analysts point to a $51B wallet tailwind from lower gas prices, tax refunds, and SNAP through year-end as underpinning the spending backdrop. US retail web traffic also accelerated to +28.1% YoY in July Week 1, led by RH and TSCO.

bullets.title: Big Bank Earnings Blowout: JPM $6.14 EPS vs $5.59 Consensus; Goldman Record Equity Trading
bullets.body: Q2 bank earnings broadly crushed estimates: JPMorgan $6.14 vs. $5.59, Wells Fargo $2.00 vs. $1.72, Bank of America $1.21 vs. $1.13. Goldman posted record $7.4B equity trading revenue. Banks weaker in European trading but holding up better than tech after strong results. Credit card spending accelerated 200bps q/q across JPM, BAC, and WFC.

bullets.title: NVDA Halves Asia Buyer List to Curb China AI Chip Diversion
bullets.body: Nvidia cut its list of authorized buyers in Singapore, Malaysia, and Japan by 50%+ amid US government pressure to prevent Chinese firms from circumventing chip export controls. Chinese technology companies have been lobbying Beijing to approve H200 sales but approval has not been granted. Jensen Huang separately denied Blackwell delivery delays, saying 800V and rack-to-rack optical interconnects remain on original timeline.

bullets.title: Data Center Moratoriums Spreading: $156B Cancelled/Delayed in 2025, $130B in 1Q26
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags $156B in data center projects cancelled or delayed in 2025 and $130B already delayed in 1Q26, driven by local opposition over power bills, environmental concerns, and quality-of-life issues. New York imposed a one-year moratorium on large new data center construction. MS sees benefits accruing to colocation REITs (EQIX OW, DLR EW) and onsite power providers (BE OW), while hyperscalers and neoclouds face the most friction.

bullets.title: Smartphone Shipments Hit 13-Year Q2 Low; Memory BOM >60% of Sub-$400 Devices
bullets.body: Global Q2 smartphone shipments fell 8% QoQ (vs. typical +2% seasonal) and -4% YoY, the first YoY decline in 10 quarters. Memory/storage now comprises 60%+ of BOM in sub-$400 devices, forcing vendors to raise prices and delay budget-tier purchases. JPM expects conditions to worsen sharply in 2H26, projecting -19% YoY vs. -1% in 1H26; budget-segment units could fall >22% YoY in full-year 2026.

bullets.title: NFIB June Optimism Hits Yearly High at 97.4, But Inflation Is #1 Concern
bullets.body: NFIB small business optimism rose 2.1pts to 97.4 in June, the largest monthly gain of 2026, with 7 of 10 components improving. Hiring plans and capital expenditure plans improved, but 21% of owners now cite inflation as their #1 problem—up 3pts MoM and the highest since October 2024—driven by fuel, tariff, insurance, and labor costs. Profit trends fell 5pts MoM despite the broad optimism.

bullets.title: AI Capex Cycle Early Innings: $2T Hyperscaler Backlog vs. $784B Spent; Software Still Underweight
bullets.body: Jefferies frames the AI capex cycle as early-innings: $2T contracted hyperscaler backlog vs. only $784B actually spent, and major cloud providers have zero available AI compute capacity for the next six months. AI accounts for <5% of total software revenue and software remains an underweight. Bear risks include 70-85% of compute used by two labs, broken unit economics on $200/month plans burning $8K-$14K in tokens, and a potential cascade if hyperscaler capex is pulled.

bullets.title: SaaS Index -12.5% YTD vs. S&P +11.3%; IGV Lagging as Enterprise IT Shifts to AI Infrastructure
bullets.body: Wolfe Research's all-SaaS index trades at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales while IGV has returned -12.5% YTD vs. the S&P 500's +11.3%. Multiple desk checks (UBS NOW, Piper security, GS TMT) confirm enterprise IT spending is stable but not accelerating, with clients redirecting discretionary budgets toward AI servers/storage rather than incremental SaaS seats. Cyber demand is the bright spot: revised to 9.6% growth in 2026 from 7.1%, with 88% of survey respondents expecting CY26 benefit.

bullets.title: AAPL Downgraded to Underweight at KeyBanc ($250 PT); Morgan Stanley Sees Price Hike as Tailwind
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded AAPL to underweight ($250 PT, 21% downside from $317) citing slowing iPhone builds, weakening US upgrades, decelerating carrier subsidies, and Services growth risk to ~7% FY27 vs. consensus ~12%. In contrast, Morgan Stanley (OW, $360 PT) sees AAPL's $200 iPhone 18 price increase driving 2-4% C3Q26 EPS upside with little change to unit demand, and views the stock as a relative safe-haven. AAPL hit record highs on Monday amid the tech selloff.

bullets.title: China June Trade Surplus Surges to $125.6B; Exports +27% YoY on AI Hardware and Tariff Front-Loading
bullets.body: China's June trade balance hit $125.62B vs. $120.10B consensus, with exports surging 27% YoY (prior 19.4%) and imports jumping 36% YoY (prior 27.4%). The Customs Vice Minister attributed export strength to AI hardware demand and confirmed the favorable trajectory is expected to continue in H2, though risks and challenges remain. Separately, China's crude oil imports fell to their lowest level in nearly a decade.

bullets.title: Japan Long-End JGB Yields Drop 15-18bps in Risk-Off Flight; BOJ Policy Floor in Focus
bullets.body: Japan's 20-year JGB yield fell as much as 16.5bps to 3.58% and the 30-year fell 18bps to 3.725% in overnight trading, a 3-standard-deviation move, as Middle East risk-off sentiment drove a safe-haven flight. The Finance Minister declined to comment on potential GPIF portfolio shifts away from overseas assets. Analysts note a modeled 37bp US yield increase for every $100B reduction in Japanese Treasury holdings.

bullets.title: META Flips to Credible AI Monetization Story; Muse Spark Priced at ~25% of OpenAI Cost
bullets.body: JPM flags META as the most important tech earnings call this quarter, noting a shift in investor debate from 'how to monetize AI' to 'how much.' META rallied ~20% in the past two weeks after unveiling Muse Spark 1.1 with API pricing at ~25% of OpenAI/Anthropic. 2027 capex is expected at $200-225B (up ~$75B YoY), with some investor estimates at $275B, and JPM models a potential equity raise if the stock sustains above $700. META closed above its 200-day MA for two consecutive days for the first time since February.

bullets.title: TSMC Expected to Report 59% YoY Q2 Net Profit; June Revenue Growth +68%
bullets.body: Sell-side consensus expects TSMC to report 59% YoY Q2 net profit on strong AI chip demand and 36% revenue growth, with June standalone revenue growth at 68%. Citi semis roundtable expects TSMC to raise 2026 sales guidance to 35%+ (vs. prior 30%+) and AI CAGR from the mid-to-high 50% range when it reports Wednesday. Investors view TSMC as the more impactful result than ASML this week, with capex guidance ($52-56B for 2026) and a potential 3-year framework as key catalysts.

bullets.title: El Niño Confirmed at 81% Odds of Very Strong Event in 4Q26; Key Commodity and Sector Exposures
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley confirms NOAA data showing 81% probability of a very strong El Niño in 4Q26 peaking in December-February and decaying into 1Q27. Key market impacts: sugar (price positive), copper (most supply-exposed), cocoa (tight supply), grains (divergent effects). Beneficiaries include scaled US food retail (WMT, COST) and South American farming; at-risk include Pacific-coast operators and chicken producers. El Niño could also pressure Middle East fertilizer and petroleum supply chains if the conflict remains unresolved.

bullets.title: Russell 2000 +19% YTD, Outperforming S&P 500 by 9.2%; Foreign Buying of US Equities at Record Pace
bullets.body: The Russell 2000 is up 19% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500 by 9.2ppts, tracking its biggest annual gain since 2003. Separately, foreign investors are purchasing US equities at the fastest pace in history. The S&P 500 Buffett Indicator (market cap/GDP) reached a record 234%, and US banks' unrealized losses rose to $316B. US public debt interest expense hit $1.35T annualized—potentially soon surpassing Social Security as the largest budget line item.
